claim: PA12 SLS tensile response depends on build orientation and part thickness.
VFM identifies constitutive parameters by combining full-field kinematics, boundary loading and virtual work.
Out-of-plane motion can bias 2D-DIC displacement/strain measurements and therefore VFM identification.
Missing deformation data near specimen edges and DIC noise can affect biaxial VFM parameter identification.
Cruciform geometry influences gauge-zone homogeneity, load transfer and constitutive characterization.
DIC reporting requires hardware, calibration and processing metadata sufficient for reproducibility.
A claim of improved identifiability requires an independent loading path or specimen not used for fitting.
